subtitle: 13 things Koreans do, ready for an interview
description: Thirteen everyday Korean customs, from bowing to noraebang, as picture cards with native audio, interview questions comparing Korea and Cambodia, and the key words.

spine.title: 노선도 · 하루 순서
spine.note: One evening with Korean coworkers: meet, eat, pay, talk, then sing.

explain.title: 한눈에 · The big picture
explain.why: Most of these customs come from two ideas: respect for older people, and 'we' before 'me'.

tiles.en: Age decides how you call people

cards.ko: 한국 사람들은 인사할 때, 고마울 때, 미안할 때 고개를 숙여요.
cards.en: Koreans bow their heads to say hello, thank you and sorry.

cards.alt: A desk name plate reading 팀장님
cards.en: At work, people are called by their title, like team leader or department head, not by name.

cards.alt: Two hands holding out a wrapped gift
cards.ko: 윗사람에게 물건을 줄 때는 두 손으로 드려요.
cards.en: You give things to an older person with two hands.

cards.alt: A table of small side dishes around a rice bowl
cards.ko: 식당에서는 반찬을 다 같이 나눠 먹어요.
cards.en: At a restaurant, everyone shares the side dishes.

cards.alt: One pot of red stew with two spoons
cards.en: Even kimchi stew is eaten together from one pot.

cards.alt: An empty bowl and a stopwatch
cards.ko: 한국 사람들은 밥을 빨리 먹는 편이에요.

cards.alt: Noodles lifted from a pot with sound lines
cards.ko: 라면을 후루룩 소리 내서 먹어도 괜찮아요.
cards.en: It's fine to slurp your ramyeon out loud.

cards.alt: A metal spoon and metal chopsticks
cards.en: In Korea, people use metal chopsticks more than wooden ones.

cards.alt: A receipt with arrows going back and forth
cards.ko: '오늘은 제가 살게요. 다음에 사 주세요.' 이렇게 돌아가면서 사요.
cards.en: 'I'll pay today. You get it next time.' People take turns paying.

cards.alt: A family under one roof with the word 우리
cards.en: People say 'our mom' and 'our company' instead of 'my'.

cards.alt: A January 1 calendar and a cake with one candle
cards.ko: 한국 나이로는 태어나면 한 살이고, 1월 1일에 모두 한 살을 더 먹어요.
cards.en: In Korean age you are one at birth, and everyone turns a year older on January 1.

cards.alt: An older friend and a younger friend calling 언니
cards.ko: 가족이 아니어도 나이가 많은 친구를 '언니', '오빠', '누나', '형'이라고 불러요.
cards.en: Even outside the family, older friends are called 언니, 오빠, 누나 or 형.

cards.alt: A karaoke screen, a microphone and music notes
cards.ko: 밥을 먹고 나서 같이 노래방에 자주 가요.
cards.en: After eating, people often go to a karaoke room together.

qa.title: 함정 · 헷갈리는 것
qa.note: The three things learners mix up most.

items.qen: Can I end sentences with -요 in an interview?
items.a: 네, 괜찮아요. 더 격식 있게 하려면 '-습니다'로 바꾸면 돼요.
items.aen: Yes, that's fine. To sound more formal, switch to -습니다.
items.why: 신기했어요 becomes 신기했습니다, 써요 becomes 씁니다. Pick one style and keep it.

items.a: 제 엄마예요. 듣는 사람 엄마가 아니에요.
items.aen: It's my own mom, not the listener's mom.
items.why: 우리 sounds warmer than 내. Use 우리 회사 for your own company too.

items.qen: Is 오빠 only for a boyfriend?
items.a: 아니요. 여자가 나이 많은 친한 남자를 부를 때 써요.
items.aen: No. A woman uses it for any older man she is close to.
items.why: A man says 형 to an older man and 누나 to an older woman. A woman says 오빠 and 언니.

qa.title: 면접에서 · In the interview
qa.small: Questions an interviewer may ask you
qa.note: Answer in your head, then tap Listen to compare.

items.q: 한국에 와서 어떤 문화가 제일 신기했어요?
items.qen: What Korean custom surprised you the most?
items.a: 밥을 정말 빨리 먹는 게 신기했어요. 처음에는 따라가기 힘들었는데 지금은 익숙해요.
items.aen: How fast people eat surprised me. At first it was hard to keep up, but now I'm used to it.

items.qen: How do you address people at a Korean company?
items.a: 이름 대신 직급에 '님'을 붙여서 불러요. 예를 들면 '팀장님'이라고 해요.
items.aen: Instead of names, you add 님 to the title. For example, you say 팀장님.

items.q: 윗사람에게 물건을 드릴 때 어떻게 해요?
items.qen: How do you hand something to an older person?
items.a: 두 손으로 드리고 고개를 살짝 숙여요.
items.aen: I give it with two hands and bow my head a little.

items.qen: Why do people say 'our company', not 'my company'?
items.a: 한국은 '나'보다 '우리'를 중요하게 생각해서 그래요. 더 친근하게 들려요.
items.aen: Because Korea puts 'we' before 'me'. It sounds friendlier.

items.qen: Do you know about Korean age?
items.a: 네, 태어나면 한 살이고 1월 1일에 한 살씩 더 먹어요. 그런데 2023년부터는 만 나이를 써요.
items.aen: Yes. You are one at birth and gain a year every January 1. But since 2023, international age is used.

items.qen: What do people usually do after a team dinner?
items.a: 노래방에 가서 같이 노래를 불러요. 코인 노래방은 싸서 자주 가요.
items.aen: They go to a karaoke room and sing together. Coin karaoke is cheap, so people go often.

items.a: 나눠서 낼 때도 있고, '오늘은 제가 살게요' 하고 돌아가면서 낼 때도 있어요.
items.aen: Sometimes we split it, and sometimes someone says 'I'll pay today' and we take turns.

items.qen: Is there a similar custom in Cambodia?
items.a: 네, 있어요. 캄보디아에서도 나이 많은 사람을 '벙'이라고 불러요. 한국의 '언니, 오빠'하고 비슷해요.
items.aen: Yes. In Cambodia we also call older people 'bong'. It's like 언니 and 오빠 in Korea.

items.q: 한국 문화하고 캄보디아 문화는 뭐가 달라요?
items.qen: How is Korean culture different from Cambodian culture?
items.a: 한국은 뭐든지 빨라요. 캄보디아는 조금 더 여유가 있어요.
items.aen: Everything in Korea is fast. Cambodia is a bit more relaxed.

qa.title: 막힐 때
qa.small: When you don't know what to say
qa.note: Add one of these to any answer and keep talking.

items.en: At first it surprised me, but now I'm used to it.

items.ko: 잘은 모르지만, 제 생각에는 존중하는 문화 같아요.
items.en: I'm not sure, but I think it's a culture of respect.

ex.en: When I see a senior, I bow my head to greet them.
At work, people are called by their title.
Team leader, here are the meeting files.
You use polite speech with seniors.
You take a business card with two hands.
You use polite speech with people you just met.

ex.ko: 반찬은 더 달라고 하면 공짜로 줘요.
ex.en: If you ask for more side dishes, they are free.
I ordered pizza and shared it with my coworkers.
I had kimchi stew for lunch.
Korea has a hurry-hurry culture.
I slurped down my ramyeon.
Metal chopsticks were a bit hard at first.
I'll get the bill.
Lunch is on me today.
We take turns buying coffee.
There's a team dinner on Friday.
My (our) company is in Gangnam.

ex.ko: 새해가 돼서 한 살 더 먹었어요.
ex.en: It's the new year, so I'm a year older.
These days international age is the official one.
Unnie, let's have lunch together.
Hyung, are you free today?
Shall we go to a karaoke room?
It is fine to go to coin karaoke alone.
At first everything amazed me.
Now I'm used to life in Korea.

full_title: 하루 순서 · One evening, start to finish

full.title: 만남 · Meeting people
full.ko: 한국 사람들은 인사할 때, 고마울 때, 미안할 때 고개를 숙여요. 회사에서는 이름 대신 '팀장님', '부장님'처럼 직급으로 불러요. 윗사람에게 물건을 줄 때는 두 손으로 드려요.
full.en: Koreans bow their heads to say hello, thank you and sorry. At work, people are called by their title, like team leader or department head, not by name. You give things to an older person with two hands.

full.title: 식사 · At the table
full.ko: 식당에서는 반찬을 다 같이 나눠 먹어요. 김치찌개도 한 냄비에서 같이 떠먹어요. 한국 사람들은 밥을 빨리 먹는 편이에요. 라면을 후루룩 소리 내서 먹어도 괜찮아요. 한국에서는 나무젓가락보다 쇠젓가락을 많이 써요.
full.en: At a restaurant, everyone shares the side dishes. Even kimchi stew is eaten together from one pot. Koreans tend to eat fast. It's fine to slurp your ramyeon out loud. In Korea, people use metal chopsticks more than wooden ones.

full.title: 계산 · Paying
full.ko: '오늘은 제가 살게요. 다음에 사 주세요.' 이렇게 돌아가면서 사요.
full.en: 'I'll pay today. You get it next time.' People take turns paying.

full.title: 대화 · How people talk
full.ko: '내 엄마' 대신 '우리 엄마', '우리 회사'라고 말해요. 한국 나이로는 태어나면 한 살이고, 1월 1일에 모두 한 살을 더 먹어요. 가족이 아니어도 나이가 많은 친구를 '언니', '오빠', '누나', '형'이라고 불러요.
full.en: People say 'our mom' and 'our company' instead of 'my'. In Korean age you are one at birth, and everyone turns a year older on January 1. Even outside the family, older friends are called 언니, 오빠, 누나 or 형.

full.title: 노래방 · After dinner
full.ko: 밥을 먹고 나서 같이 노래방에 자주 가요.
full.en: After eating, people often go to a karaoke room together.

station_en: Thirteen Korean customs, from bowing to noraebang, to talk about in an interview.
